name: Benign Ovarian Masses, Mature Cystic Teratoma and Adnexal Torsion

reference.source: Gynaecology by Ten Teachers 21st Edition / ACOG Practice Bulletin on Adnexal Masses
clinicalPearls: Mature cystic teratoma dermoid cyst contains all three germ cell layers and features hyperechoic Rokitansky nodule
Functional follicular cysts represent unruptured graafian follicles and resolve spontaneously within two menstrual cycles
Adnexal torsion presents with acute unilateral lower abdominal pain with nausea, requiring urgent surgical detorsion
Surgical untwisting of a torsed ischemic-appearing ovary preserves ovarian function and does not increase thromboembolic risk
Endometrioma ground-glass appearance on ultrasound results from cyclic bleeding into ectopic endometrial ovarian implants
reference.pathophysiology: Benign ovarian masses encompass physiological cysts arising from ovulatory failure, benign germ cell neoplasms (mature cystic teratoma), and surface epithelial tumors (serous and mucinous cystadenomas). Adnexal torsion occurs when an enlarged mobile ovary (typically 5-10 cm) twists around its infundibulopelvic and utero-ovarian suspensory axis, initially occluding venous drainage, causing massive stromal edema and hemorrhage, followed by arterial compromise and gangrene.
additionalInvestigations: Transvaginal and transabdominal pelvic ultrasound with color and spectral Doppler
Serum quantitative beta-hCG to exclude ectopic pregnancy
Serum tumor markers (CA-125, AFP, beta-hCG, LDH) in complex masses
